claims.text: Ti35Ni35Cr10Al10Mo10 is a five-element, titanium–nickel-primary composition in which every element is present at 5–35 at%.
Casting and/or high-temperature solution treatment can produce a single-phase BCC/B2 solid solution in Ti35Ni35Cr10Al10Mo10.
Solutionizing the proposed alloy at approximately 1100°C maintains a single-phase solid solution.
A two-step solution-and-aging treatment can produce a finer and more uniformly distributed precipitate population than treatment without the aging step.
Aging near 800°C for 1–2 hours followed by controlled cooling will produce the desired precipitate dispersion in Ti35Ni35Cr10Al10Mo10.
Optimizing aging time, temperature, and cooling rate can regulate precipitate size and distribution and limit coarsening.
The treatment will create nanometer-scale, uniformly dispersed, coherent Ti2Ni or sigma precipitates in the proposed alloy matrix.
Fine precipitates obstruct dislocation glide at elevated temperature.
Fine precipitates obstruct grain-boundary sliding at elevated temperature.
Precipitate coherency preserves ductility by avoiding stress concentrators and premature failure.
The aged alloy will have higher elevated-temperature yield strength than the same alloy in the as-cast or solely solution-treated condition.
The aged alloy will have a lower creep strain rate and delayed onset of creep deformation.
The predicted mechanical benefit extends across testing temperatures from 700°C to 900°C.
The effect should be significant throughout compositions having five elements at 5–35 at% each.
Departures from the proposed aging parameters may produce coarsened or inhomogeneous precipitates and compromise mechanical performance.
In a related Al–Nb–Ti–V alloy containing Ni or Co, heat treatment at 1100°C for 1 hour formed homogeneously distributed sigma particles in a BCC matrix and enhanced yield strength.
Sigma and Ti2Ni phases have been observed in a Ti–Nb–Cr–V–Ni–Al refractory high-entropy alloy.
The exact optimum aging conditions and the magnitude of the resulting yield-strength and creep improvements remain uncertain.
